subject: Dedicated capacity demo request — tail latency & routing
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@fastatlas.com>
To: Redwood Inference Sales <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity demo request — tail latency & routing

Hi Marcus,

We just self-signed up and ran a few tests with the hosted API — looks promising. We’re evaluating Redwood for a production path that will use dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) because our workload requires:
- 2000 sustained QPS (short text inference)
- 99.9th-percentile latency <= 120ms at peak
- Strong tail-latency stability during bursty traffic (advertising auction windows)

Can we schedule a focused demo on Dedicated capacity that covers: routing policies, fallback model variants, autoscale behavior for bursts, and any pre-warm or KV-caching recommendations? I attached a sample load profile (load_profile.csv) to give a sense of our traffic pattern.

Prefer next week (US/PDT). Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, FastAtlas
ops@fastatlas.com

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the load profile, that helps a lot. Ben (cc’d) runs our Dedicated intake for high-QPS customers and will join the call.

Two quick questions before we lock time:
1) Is 2,000 QPS sustained across a single region or multi-region?
2) What’s your typical sequence length / prompt size (tokens)? Short completion only?

Available windows (PDT):
- Tue 06/22 10:00–11:00
- Wed 06/23 14:00–15:00
- Thu 06/24 08:30–09:00 (short sync)

We’ll prepare a short runbook and a canary-fallback flow to walk through routing and model variants. If any of those times work, share calendar availability and we’ll send an invite.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — answers below:
1) Single region for now (us-west) but we may expand to multi-region next quarter.
2) Very short prompts: median 12 tokens, median completion 8 tokens; lots of rapid-fire requests (ads bids).

We can do Tue 06/22 10:00–11:00 PDT. I attached the load_profile.csv with an hourly breakdown and a separate sheet that shows peak bursts (60s windows).

Also, is it possible to get a pre-demo link where we can run 1000 requests against a dedicated-qualification endpoint? Would like to sanity-check latency numbers before the call.

—Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Elena — great, thanks for confirming the slot. Attaching our intake runbook (dedicated-demo-runbook.pdf) — it includes a pre-call checklist that we’ll use to size the Dedicated pool and pick an autoscale curve.

A few pre-call asks (small checklist):
- Confirm expected concurrency per client (we assume 200 concurrent workers to hit 2000 QPS; let us know if different)
- Any special networking (private VPC) or egress constraints?
- Do you require strict FIFO routing or can we apply request-level routing based on latency vs cost policy?

About the pre-demo load: we can provision a temporary qualification endpoint in our staging Dedicated environment. It’s not identical to production, but it should surface tail-latency modes. If you’re comfortable, send a short list of IPs we should whitelist and we’ll provision creds + a Postman collection.

Attaching: dedicated-demo-runbook.pdf

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise SDR, Redwood Inference
